newsitem.title: INDIA: India bank rate cut to hurt power firms' profits.
newsitem.headline: India bank rate cut to hurt power firms' profits.

text.p: The central bank's decision to cut the benchmark bank rate last week will hurt the profitability of five private Indian power companies during the next financial year, company officials said on Tuesday.
The five firms are BSES Ltd, Tata Electric Companies, Ahmedabad Electricity Company Ltd, Surat Electricity Company Ltd and CESC Ltd.
According to India's Electricity Supply Act, private electricity licensees are allowed to earn a fixed rate of five percentage points above the bank rate on their capital base.
The act specificies that the bank rate prevailing on April 1 of the financial year be used to calculate the return.
The five companies will each earn a return of 17 percent on the capital base during 1997/98 (April-March) as the bank rate on April 1, 1997, was 12 percent.
The Reserve Bank of India has since reduced the bank rate by two percentage points to 10 percent.
This will mean a reduced return of 15 percent for 1998/99.
The Federation of Electricity Undertakings is taking up the matter with the government, a BSES official told Reuters.
"The act gives the government the power to notify that licensees' return will not be linked to the bank rate," an official of BSES said.
"Independent power producers are already allowed 16 percent irrespective of the bank rate," he added.
Analysts expect the government to alter the criteria to encourage private producers of power.
"A fixed return is not very encouraging," said Gaurav Rastogi, analyst at Classic Share & Stock Broking Services.
"I expect the government to overhaul the entire criteria."

In addition to a fixed return of 16 percent, independent power producers are entitled to an incentive return of 0.7 percent for each percentage point improvement in the plant load factor above a threshold level.
